name: Stelceram-7
description: Stelceram-7 is a CNT-reinforced silicon carbide ceramic matrix composite developed jointly by Crucible Industries and Tessera Materials, produced through a hot-press sintering process that infiltrates a porous SiC preform with aligned carbon nanotubes, bridging cracks at the nanoscale before they can propagate. The material achieves the hardness and thermal stability of advanced ceramics while eliminating the catastrophic brittle failure mode that makes conventional ceramics unreliable under impact — Stelceram-7 fails progressively, absorbing energy as it does. It operates continuously to 2,200°C and is nearly impervious to chemical attack.
story_hooks: Stelceram-7 armor plate is rated against specific threat levels — someone has been quietly testing ammunition specifically designed to exploit the material's semi-conductive properties to deliver an electrical pulse through it.

A black-market supply of Stelceram-7 tiles is available at a fraction of the market price; they're genuine material, but they've been recovered from a crash site and may have experienced thermal stresses that compromised their structure invisibly.
Tessera Materials and Crucible Industries are in a licensing dispute over Stelceram-7 production rights — manufacturing is at risk of interruption just as a major defense contract depends on supply.
